q: AI 编码面试里的沟通为什么比传统面试更难？
q_en: Why is communication in an AI coding interview harder than in a traditional interview?
options: 因为必须背诵固定提示词
因为面试官看不到你的屏幕
因为你同时要对 AI 和对面试官两条线沟通
因为 AI 输出的内容不允许被讨论
why: 决定性因素是你要同时维持两条沟通线——AI 和面试官；只顾 AI 会让面试官读不到你的判断过程。
why_en: AI coding interviews are harder to communicate through because you must run two conversations at once, with the AI and with the interviewer.
diagram:
flowchart TD
  Candidate[Candidate] --> Interviewer[Interviewer]
  Candidate --> AI[AI tool]
  AI --> Candidate
  Candidate --> Code[Codebase]
  Code --> Interviewer
options_en: Because you have to recite a fixed set of prompts.
Because the interviewer can't see your screen.
Because you have to communicate on two channels at once, to the AI and to the interviewer.
Because AI output is off-limits for discussion.
optionMeanings: 把沟通难度归因为背模板提示词。
假设面试官看不到你的操作过程。
把沟通难度归因为要同时维护两条对话线。
假设 AI 输出是不能讨论的黑箱。
optionScenarioImpacts: 背模板不能应对具体代码上下文，帮不上真实沟通。
事实相反：面试官能看到提示和输出，只是看不到你的思路。
点出了两条线同时维护才是难度来源。
误解了规则：解释 AI 输出正是沟通该做的事。
optionDirectness: 背诵不是沟通技巧，遇到没背过的场景就会露馅。
前提有误：不是看不到屏幕，是看不到你的思路。
这条线索决定了你要主动说出思路，而不是只操作 AI。
前提有误：讨论 AI 输出正是加分项，不是禁区。
optionMeanings_en: This blames the difficulty on reciting template prompts.
This assumes the interviewer can't see what you're doing.
This blames the difficulty on maintaining two conversation threads at once.
This assumes AI output is a black box you can't discuss.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Reciting a template doesn't handle real code context, so it doesn't help.
The opposite is true: the interviewer sees the prompts and output, just not your thinking.
It names the real source of difficulty: keeping two channels alive at once.
It misreads the rules: explaining AI output is exactly what good communication looks like.
optionDirectness_en: Reciting isn't a communication skill, it breaks down outside the memorized case.
Wrong premise: it's not the screen that's hidden, it's your thought process.
This is the actual reason you must voice your thinking, not just operate the AI.
Wrong premise: discussing AI output is a plus signal, not off-limits.

scenario: 你准备让 AI 给 Order 类实现输入校验。
scenario_en: You are about to ask the AI to add input validation to the Order class.
q: 提示 AI 前，最应该先对面试官说什么？
q_en: Before prompting the AI, what should you say to the interviewer first?
options: “我要给 Order 加校验，先查空字段和数量范围。”
“我先让 AI 随便试着写写看，看它怎么处理。”
“等它写完了，我再跟你解释我的思路。”
“不说什么，先直接开始打字提示它。”
why: 决定性约束是面试官只能看到提示和输出、看不到你的思路；先说意图能把后续内容放进上下文。
why_en: State your intent before prompting so the interviewer can follow your plan instead of just watching you type.
whenOtherWins: 如果只是改一个显而易见的一行 typo，可以边改边说一句，不需要完整铺陈。
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Intent[State intent] --> Prompt[Prompt AI]
  Prompt --> Review[Review output]
  Review --> Explain[Explain next step]
options_en: I'm going to add validation to Order, checking null fields and quantity range first.
I'll just let the AI take a random first pass and see what it does.
I'll wait until it's done, then explain my thinking to you.
I won't say anything, I'll just start typing the prompt.
tradeoff: 提示前先说明意图 vs 直接开始打字
optionMeanings: 先公开具体校验范围的意图声明。
把决策权交给 AI 随机尝试。
把说明推迟到 AI 写完之后。
完全跳过意图声明。
optionScenarioImpacts: 面试官能提前知道校验范围，跟上后续每一步。
面试官只能等结果出来才知道你在做什么。
面试官全程只能看操作，事后才补上下文。
面试官从头到尾看不到你的判断依据。
optionDirectness: 三秒声明换来面试官全程可跟随的上下文。
只适合改一行显而易见的 typo，不适合完整功能。
输出量大时可以事后补充细节，但不能替代提示前的意图声明。
只在改动极小、几乎不需要解释时才勉强够用。
optionMeanings_en: Stating the specific validation scope up front.
Handing the decision to a random first AI attempt.
Delaying the explanation until after the AI finishes.
Skipping the intent statement entirely.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: The interviewer knows the validation scope ahead of time and can follow each step.
The interviewer only learns what you're doing once the result appears.
The interviewer can only watch actions and gets context after the fact.
The interviewer never sees your reasoning at any point.
optionDirectness_en: A three-second statement buys context the interviewer can follow the whole way.
Fine for an obvious one-line typo fix, not for a full feature.
Useful when output is large, but it can't replace stating intent before prompting.
Barely acceptable only when the change is tiny and needs no explanation.

q: 把推荐的 AI 编码沟通节奏排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the recommended AI coding communication rhythm in the correct order:
steps: 审阅 AI 输出并说出是否符合预期
继续下一步或重新提示
说明你接下来要做什么
向 AI 发出具体提示
why: 有效节奏是先声明意图，再提示 AI，然后公开审阅结果，最后决定继续或修正。
why_en: The useful rhythm is state intent, prompt the AI, review aloud, then continue or correct course.
tradeoff: 先声明意图再行动 vs 先动手后解释
diagram:
flowchart LR
  SayPlan[Say plan] --> AskAI[Ask AI]
  AskAI --> Narrate[Narrate wait]
  Narrate --> Review[Review output]
  Review --> Next[State next move]

q: AI 生成代码后，哪些口头反馈是好信号？（多选）
q_en: After the AI generates code, which spoken reactions are good signals? (Select all that apply.)
options: “AI 写了，所以肯定对。”
“这符合我的目标，它检查了 null 字段和数量。”
“它用了异常，但项目里用 error object，我会重新提示。”
“这段很多，我先读一遍确认。”
why: 这些反馈展示你在验证、纠偏和主动审查；盲目接受 AI 输出是负面信号。
why_en: Good narration shows that you verify, correct, and review AI output rather than accepting it blindly.
options_en: The AI wrote it, so it must be correct.
This matches my goal, it checks for null fields and validates quantity.
It used exceptions, but this codebase uses error objects, so I'll reprompt.
This is a lot of code, let me read through it first to confirm.
optionMeanings: 把结果好坏归因于 AI 本身而非你的核验。
确认输出是否命中你已声明的校验目标。
发现风格不符并主动要求重新生成。
承认大段输出需要先读完再判断。
optionScenarioImpacts: 跳过核验，面试官会认为你在盲目接受。
证明你在核对具体校验点，不是走过场。
展示你能发现代码库风格冲突并纠偏。
展示你不会因为代码量大就跳过审阅。
optionDirectness: 唯一站不住脚的判断：输出正确与否不取决于是谁写的。
点名具体校验点的确认，是可评估的核验信号。
发现风格冲突并重提示，是纠偏能力的直接证据。
承认需要时间审阅，是诚实且专业的信号。
optionMeanings_en: Attributing correctness to the AI itself rather than your own verification.
Confirming the output hits the validation goal you stated.
Spotting a style mismatch and asking for a reprompt.
Admitting a large output needs a read-through before judgment.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Skipping verification makes the interviewer think you accept output blindly.
It proves you're checking specific validation points, not just going through motions.
It shows you can catch a codebase style conflict and correct it.
It shows you won't skip review just because the output is long.
optionDirectness_en: The one claim that doesn't hold up: correctness doesn't depend on who wrote it.
Naming a specific check point is evaluable verification.
Catching a style conflict and reprompting is direct evidence of self-correction.
Admitting you need time to review is an honest, professional signal.

q: AI 编码面试里，面试官更应该被当成什么角色？
q_en: In an AI coding interview, what role should you treat the interviewer as?
options: 只看最终结果、不参与过程的考官
不能被打扰的旁观者
可以被 AI 取代的角色
和你一起结对写代码的伙伴
why: AI 编码面试更像结对编程，面试官需要持续听到你的意图、判断和修正才能评估你。
why_en: Treat the interviewer like a pair partner who needs to keep hearing your intent, judgment, and corrections.
options_en: An examiner who only looks at the final result and ignores the process.
A bystander you should not interrupt.
A role the AI can substitute for.
A pair-programming partner working alongside you.
tradeoff: 把面试官当结对伙伴持续沟通 vs 当考官只交最终结果
optionMeanings: 把评估窗口收窄成只看结果的模型。
把面试官当成不该打断的旁观者。
误以为讲清楚给 AI 听就够了。
把面试官当成需要持续同步的搭档。
optionScenarioImpacts: 你会倾向沉默写代码，到最后才展示成果。
你会不敢开口说思路，错过评估窗口。
面试官听到的是你和 AI 的对话，不是你的判断。
你会持续讲意图、判断和修正，让评估全程可见。
optionDirectness: 只适合纯笔试式评审，不适合边讲边写的面试形式。
只在你完全不需要任何反馈的极端场景下才成立。
把判断权交给 AI，面试官学不到你的思路。
结对式沟通让面试官全程跟上你的意图和修正。
optionMeanings_en: This narrows the evaluation window to a results-only model.
This treats the interviewer as a bystander you shouldn't interrupt.
This mistakenly assumes talking to the AI is communication enough.
This treats the interviewer as a partner who needs constant syncing.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: You'd tend to code silently and only reveal the result at the end.
You'd hesitate to voice your thinking and lose the evaluation window.
The interviewer hears your conversation with the AI, not your judgment.
You keep narrating intent, judgment, and corrections so evaluation stays visible.
optionDirectness_en: Fits a pure written exam, not a talk-while-you-build interview.
Only holds in the extreme case where no feedback is ever needed.
Handing judgment to the AI means the interviewer learns nothing about you.
Pair-style communication keeps the interviewer following your intent and fixes throughout.

q: 补全 AI 编码面试的推荐沟通节奏：
q_en: Complete the recommended communication rhythm for an AI coding interview:
text: 有效沟通节奏是：先说明{{意图}}，再提示 AI，接着公开{{审阅输出}}，最后说明{{下一步}}。
why: 这个节奏让面试官持续看到你在做决策，而不是把判断外包给 AI。
why_en: This rhythm keeps the interviewer aware that you are making the decisions, not outsourcing judgment to the AI.

scenario: AI 在结构化平台里响应很慢，屏幕上出现加载动画，你在等待生成结果。
scenario_en: The AI is slow to respond in a structured platform, and you are waiting on a loading spinner.
q: AI 还在生成时，这段等待时间最好怎么用？
q_en: While the AI is still generating, how should you best use the waiting time?
options: 沉默盯着加载动画
打开无关网页放松一下
向面试官讲你的方案、预期输出或边界条件
不断重复提交同一个提示
why: 等待时间正好用来填补空白——讲方案、预期输出或边界条件，正是面试官想听的判断和取舍。
why_en: Use AI wait time to talk through your approach, expected output, and edge cases instead of sitting in silence.
whenOtherWins: 如果你已经说清方案，也可以利用等待时间阅读下一步代码或写测试草案。
options_en: Sit in silence staring at the loading spinner.
Open an unrelated webpage to relax.
Talk the interviewer through your approach, expected output, or edge cases.
Keep resubmitting the same prompt over and over.
tradeoff: 用等待时间讲思路 vs 沉默等结果
optionMeanings: 把等待当成纯粹的空白时间。
用等待时间做和面试无关的事。
把等待时间转成口头推理时间。
误以为重复提交能让生成变快。
optionScenarioImpacts: 面试官会觉得不适，也拿不到你的推理过程。
会被判断为脱离面试状态、不专注。
把本来的空白填成面试官想听的判断和取舍。
浪费等待时间，也不会让 AI 更快回应。
optionDirectness: 只在你已经说完全部思路、真的无话可说时才勉强能接受。
任何时候都不该用来处理和题目无关的事。
等待越久，讲解思路带来的收益越明显。
重复提交对生成速度没有帮助，纯粹浪费时间。
optionMeanings_en: Treating wait time as pure dead air.
Using wait time on something unrelated to the interview.
Turning wait time into spoken reasoning time.
Wrongly assuming resubmitting speeds up generation.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: The interviewer feels uncomfortable and gets none of your reasoning.
It reads as disengagement from the interview.
It fills the dead air with exactly the judgment the interviewer wants to hear.
It wastes the wait time without making the AI respond any faster.
optionDirectness_en: Barely acceptable only once you've already said everything there is to say.
Never appropriate for interview-unrelated activity.
The longer the wait, the more this narration pays off.
Resubmitting has no effect on generation speed, it's pure waste.

q: AI 生成期间可以并行做哪些有价值的事？（多选）
q_en: What useful work can you do in parallel while the AI is generating? (Select all that apply.)
options: 阅读下一阶段可能需要的代码
草拟当前步骤的测试用例
完全停下等 AI
思考边界条件
why: 并行阅读、写测试草案和想边界情况能让你更快，也让面试官看到你没有被动等待。
why_en: Reading ahead, drafting tests, and thinking through edge cases turn AI wait time into productive interview time.
options_en: Read the code you'll likely need for the next stage.
Sketch out test cases for the current step.
Stop completely and just wait for the AI.
Think through edge cases.
optionMeanings: 提前读下一阶段要用到的代码。
利用等待时间先写测试草案。
把等待当成必须完全静止的时间。
利用等待时间提前想边界情况。
optionScenarioImpacts: 下一步提示 AI 时你已经有上下文准备。
AI 输出后可以立刻用测试验证，而不是现想。
错过并行处理的效率窗口，也显得被动。
边界情况提前想清楚，减少后续返工。
optionDirectness: 生成期间做这件事几乎没有额外成本。
测试草案可以在输出后立刻拿来验证。
唯一该避免的做法：完全被动等待没有任何收益。
边界情况通常需要独立思考时间，等待期正合适。
optionMeanings_en: Reading ahead the code you'll need for the next stage.
Using wait time to draft test cases.
Treating wait time as a period you must sit completely still.
Using wait time to think through edge cases in advance.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: You already have context ready when you prompt for the next step.
You can verify with tests immediately after the output arrives.
You miss the efficiency window and look passive.
Edge cases are settled early, cutting later rework.
optionDirectness_en: This costs almost nothing extra during generation.
Draft tests are ready to run the moment output arrives.
The one thing to avoid: passive waiting has zero payoff.
Edge cases usually need standalone thought, and wait time fits perfectly.

q: 长时间盯着 AI 加载动画不说话，最大的问题是什么？
q_en: What is the biggest problem with staring at the AI loading spinner in silence for a long time?
options: 面试官分不清你是在想、卡住还是干等
AI 会因此生成更差的代码
测试会自动判定失败
代码库会因此丢失上下文
why: 沉默本身不一定错，但不解释会让面试官失去你的思维轨迹，沟通成本立刻上升。
why_en: Unframed silence leaves the interviewer unable to tell whether you are thinking, stuck, or just waiting.
options_en: The interviewer can't tell if you're thinking, stuck, or just waiting passively.
The AI will generate worse code as a result.
Tests will automatically fail.
The codebase will lose context.
optionMeanings: 沉默本身没有信息量，面试官只能猜测状态。
把沉默和代码质量下降错误挂钩。
把沉默和测试结果错误挂钩。
把沉默和代码库状态错误挂钩。
optionScenarioImpacts: 评估窗口消失，沟通成本立刻上升。
沉默不会改变 AI 的生成质量，这不是真实机制。
测试通过与否只看代码，和你说不说话无关。
代码库上下文不会因为你沉默而丢失。
optionDirectness: 唯一站得住脚的解释：沉默让状态判断失去依据。
这是无关联的因果，AI 生成不受你说话与否影响。
测试失败只取决于代码逻辑，不取决于你的沉默。
上下文丢失是技术问题，不是沟通行为造成的。
optionMeanings_en: Silence itself carries no information, so the interviewer can only guess.
This wrongly links silence to worse code quality.
This wrongly links silence to test outcomes.
This wrongly links silence to codebase state.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: The evaluation window disappears and communication cost rises immediately.
Silence doesn't change AI generation quality — that's not how it works.
Test results depend only on the code, not on whether you're talking.
Codebase context doesn't vanish because you're quiet.
optionDirectness_en: The one explanation that holds: silence removes the basis for judging your state.
This is an unrelated causal claim; talking doesn't affect AI generation.
Test failure depends only on code logic, not your silence.
Context loss is a technical issue, not caused by staying quiet.

scenario: 你在处理图问题时卡在如何检测和处理 cycle（环），已经原地绕了一会儿。
scenario_en: You are working on a graph problem and have been stuck for a while on detecting and handling cycles.
q: 发现自己卡住时，最好的沟通方式是什么？
q_en: When you realize you are stuck, what is the best way to communicate?
options: 继续沉默消耗时间
让 AI 随机重写整个方案
假装已经解决，跳过这一步
说清楚卡在哪里，并向面试官请求建议
why: 请求帮助是协作而非失败；面试官更愿意看到你暴露阻塞点并继续推进，而不是沉默硬扛。
why_en: Naming a specific blocker and asking for help is collaboration and keeps the interview moving forward.
whenOtherWins: 如果你刚形成清晰假设，可以先用一分钟验证；超过这个时间就该显式沟通。
options_en: Stay silent and keep burning time.
Have the AI randomly rewrite the whole solution.
Pretend it's already solved and move on.
Name exactly where you're stuck and ask the interviewer for suggestions.
tradeoff: 主动说出卡点求助 vs 独自沉默消耗时间
optionMeanings: 把卡住的状态藏起来，独自消耗时间。
把方向判断完全交给随机重写。
用假装掩盖真实的卡点。
把卡点具体化并请求外部建议。
optionScenarioImpacts: 面试官只看到你原地打转，评估不到任何进展。
随机重写可能偏离已经验证过的部分方案。
假装很快会被追问细节戳穿，可信度受损。
阻塞点被摆到台面上，面试官能顺着一起想。
optionDirectness: 唯一没有信息增量的做法，纯粹浪费时间。
只有在现有方案已确认整体错误时才该整体重写。
短期内可能蒙混过关，但经不起追问。
求助是协作信号，不是能力不足的证明。
optionMeanings_en: Hiding the stuck state and burning time alone.
Handing the direction decision entirely to a random rewrite.
Using pretense to mask the real blocker.
Making the blocker concrete and asking for outside input.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: The interviewer only sees you spinning in place with no measurable progress.
A random rewrite risks discarding parts of the plan already validated.
Pretense collapses under a follow-up question and hurts credibility.
The blocker is now on the table, so the interviewer can think it through with you.
optionDirectness_en: The one option that adds zero information, pure time waste.
Only makes sense once you've confirmed the whole approach is wrong.
Might bluff short-term, but doesn't survive a follow-up question.
Asking for help is a collaboration signal, not proof of weakness.

termDefinitions.meaning: 图论中指从一个节点出发、沿边走一圈能回到自己的路径，即环路。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cycle is a path in a graph that starts and ends at the same node, forming a loop.

q: 补全转向（换方案）时应该说出的信息：
q_en: Complete what you should say when pivoting to a different approach:
text: 改变方向时要说明旧方案为什么{{不成立}}，新方案解决了什么{{约束}}，以及下一步怎么{{执行}}。
why: 解释转向能把看似混乱的重写变成可评估的适应能力。
why_en: Explaining a pivot turns a rewrite into evidence of adaptive problem solving.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Stuck[Stuck] --> Name[Name issue]
  Name --> Pivot[State pivot]
  Pivot --> NewPlan[New plan]
  NewPlan --> Continue[Continue]

scenario: 你发现当前暴力方案在大输入下会超时，准备换成堆优化（heap-based）方案。
scenario_en: You realize the current brute-force approach will time out on large inputs, so you are switching to a heap-based approach.
q: 换方案时，最好的口头说明是哪一句？
q_en: When changing approaches, which spoken explanation is best?
options: “暴力方案在大输入下复杂度太高，我改用 heap 方案。”
“我全部删掉，从头重新写一遍。”
“AI 说该换，我就跟着换了。”
“这里的实现应该差不多能用。”

optionMeanings: 同时点出问题、原因和替代方案的转向说明。

options_en: It's always worse than never making a mistake at all.
It means the candidate can't use the AI independently.
Recognizing the issue and explaining the pivot is actually a strong signal.
It means everything done before that point is wasted.
optionMeanings: 把犯错本身当成绝对减分项。

探索过程本身也在积累对问题的理解，不是浪费。
optionMeanings_en: Treating any mistake as an absolute deduction.
Attributing a wrong turn to being unable to use the AI.
Treating recognize-and-pivot as a positive signal.
Treating all prior work as invalid.

Recognizing the issue and pivoting clearly proves judgment and adaptability.

q: 编码时，兼顾速度与清晰度的最佳叙述粒度是什么？
q_en: While coding, what narration level best balances speed and clarity?
options: 逐字描述每个按键
只在决策、意外和修正这些拐点说明
完全不解释，只保证写得快
每写一行代码就读一遍
why: 高频细节拖慢节奏，完全沉默又失去评估窗口；只在拐点叙述能兼顾两者。
why_en: Narrating only decisions, surprises, and corrections balances speed with visible reasoning.
options_en: Narrate every single keystroke.
Narrate only at inflection points: decisions, surprises, and corrections.
Explain nothing at all and just optimize for typing speed.
Read every line of code out loud as you write it.
tradeoff: 只讲拐点 vs 逐字播报
optionMeanings: 把叙述粒度细化到每个按键。

拐点叙述是速度和可见思考之间的平衡点。

optionMeanings_en: Narrating down to every single keystroke.
Focusing narration on decisions, surprises, and corrections.
Dropping narration to zero.
Setting narration granularity to every line of code.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Signal drowns in keyboard noise and the interviewer misses the point.

You're fast, but the interviewer loses the evaluation window.
Reading every line slows the pace and most lines carry no decision value.
optionDirectness_en: The one granularity that never pays off in any scenario.
Inflection-point narration is the balance point between speed and visible thinking.
Barely acceptable only if you've already synced another way just before.

scenario: 你在稳定推进代码，没有卡住，也没有需要特别强调的决策。
scenario_en: You are making steady coding progress, with no blocker and no major decision to call out.
q: 活跃编码时，怎样的进度叙述频率最合适？
q_en: During active coding, what progress narration frequency works best?
options: 每敲几个字符就播报一次
大约每 30 到 60 秒说一句在做什么、为什么
只在写完全部代码后总结一次

why: 30-60 秒是经验性节奏参考、不是公式算出来的；太密会打断打字流，太疏又会显得失联。
why_en: Roughly one narration every thirty to sixty seconds is a practical guideline, not a formula, that keeps the interviewer aligned without interrupting your flow.
options_en: Announce progress after every few characters typed.
Say what you're doing and why roughly every 30 to 60 seconds.
Only summarize once, after all the code is written.

会让系统依赖「完全不说，靠面试官自己看代码判断」这个前提。

q: 编码过程中，哪些时刻最值得主动说出来？（多选）
q_en: During coding, which moments are most worth saying out loud? (Select all that apply.)
options: AI 输出和你的预期不一致

why_en: The interviewer needs decisions, mismatches, and corrections, not keystroke-level commentary.
options_en: The AI's output doesn't match what you expected.
Every time you type a single punctuation mark.
You're about to start the next implementation step.
You realize the algorithm or data structure needs to change.

把叙述粒度细到标点符号级别。
标记即将开始的新步骤。

The one granularity to avoid in any scenario.
A step change is a natural, low-cost narration point.
An algorithm or structure change is an inflection point affecting all following code.

scenario: 你需要安静想十几秒，确认当前算法能否覆盖边界情况。
scenario_en: You need to think quietly for ten or so seconds to confirm whether the current algorithm covers edge cases.
q: 这时最合适的处理方式是什么？
q_en: What is the best way to handle this moment?
options: 直接沉默，让面试官自己猜
立刻让 AI 生成新方案
说“我想一下这个边界情况”，然后短暂停顿
跳过边界情况，先往下写
why: 一句框定语能把沉默变成可理解的思考时间，避免面试官误以为你卡住或走神。
why_en: A short framing sentence turns silence into an understandable thinking pause instead of ambiguous dead air.
whenOtherWins: 如果你已经有可运行测试，可以边说边跑测试，用结果帮助思考。
options_en: Go silent and let the interviewer guess what's happening.
Immediately have the AI generate a new approach.
Say 'let me think about this edge case' and pause briefly.
Skip the edge case and keep moving.
tradeoff: 一句框定语再沉默 vs 直接沉默不说明

用生成新方案代替独立思考的时间。

跳过边界情况本身，回避而非思考。
optionScenarioImpacts: 面试官分不清你是在想、卡住还是走神。
还没想清楚就重新生成，容易越改越乱。

只在边界情况明显不影响正确性时才能跳过。
optionMeanings_en: Treating thinking time as silent dead air.
Substituting a new generation for actual independent thought.
Using a framing sentence to make silence understandable.
Skipping the edge case itself, avoiding rather than thinking.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: The interviewer can't tell if you're thinking, stuck, or distracted.

The interviewer clearly knows this is a normal thinking pause.
The edge case gets skipped and may surface as a bug later.
optionDirectness_en: Barely skippable only right after you've already framed a pause once.
Only worth it once you've confirmed the whole approach is unworkable.
A few seconds of framing buys clear silence at almost no cost.
Only skippable when the edge case clearly doesn't affect correctness.

scenario: 你要让 AI 实现搜索函数，需要让面试官清楚你选的是 BFS，而不是把决策交给 AI。
scenario_en: You want the AI to implement a search function, and the interviewer needs to know you chose BFS rather than handing the decision to the AI.
q: 哪组“口头说明 + 提示”最能体现你在主导决策？
q_en: Which pair of spoken framing and prompt best shows that you are driving the decision?
options: 说明：我看看 AI 会怎么处理。提示：“solve this”
说明：用 BFS 找最短路径。提示：在 Grid 上实现 BFS 并返回坐标路径。

说明：AI 应该知道怎么做。提示：“写一个复杂的解法”
why: 先公开你的策略，再把同一策略写进提示，能让 AI 输出贴合方案，同时向面试官展示你在做决策。
why_en: State your strategy out loud and put the same strategy in the prompt so the AI executes your decision, not its own.
whenOtherWins: 如果算法选择还没确定，可以先说明你在比较 BFS、DFS 或 Dijkstra，再决定后提示。
options_en: Framing: let's see what the AI does. Prompt: 'solve this.'
Framing: I'll use BFS for the shortest path. Prompt: implement BFS on Grid and return the coordinate path.
Framing: none. Prompt: 'make it work.'
Framing: the AI should already know. Prompt: 'write a complex solution.'
tradeoff: 先说策略再写进提示 vs 不说明直接丢给 AI 决定
optionMeanings: 用被动语气把决策权交给 AI 自行判断。
先声明算法选择，再把同一约束写进提示。
完全不给上下文，只留一句模糊指令。
假设 AI 会自己猜到你要的复杂方案。
optionScenarioImpacts: AI 可能选出你无法在面试里讲清楚的方案。
AI 输出直接落在 BFS 实现上，面试官也看到你的判断。

optionDirectness: 只有在你确实还没想清楚算法、想先看 AI 建议时才该用，且要说明这是在探索。

空指令几乎总会导致返工，任何场景都不推荐。
“复杂解法”不是可执行约束，AI 无法据此写出你要的代码。
optionMeanings_en: Using a passive framing that hands the decision to the AI.
Stating the algorithm choice first, then encoding the same constraint in the prompt.
Giving no context at all, just one vague instruction.
Assuming the AI will guess the complex solution you want.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: The AI may pick an approach you can't defend clearly in the interview.
The AI's output lands directly on a BFS implementation, and the interviewer sees your judgment.
The AI might pick any algorithm, drifting from your actual intent.
With no constraint, the AI's output direction is likely to miss what you expected.
optionDirectness_en: Only appropriate when you're genuinely still exploring and say so explicitly.
Keeping strategy consistent between speech and prompt is the standard move here.

termDefinitions.meaning: 广度优先搜索，按层从起点向外扩展，用于无权图找最短路径。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: BFS, Breadth-First Search, explores a graph layer by layer from the start node and finds shortest paths in unweighted graphs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 深度优先搜索，沿一条路径尽量往前探索，走到底再回溯。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DFS, Depth-First Search, explores as far as possible along one path before backtracking.

termDefinitions.meaning: 处理带权图最短路径的经典算法，每次扩展当前已知代价最小的节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dijkstra's Algorithm finds shortest paths in a weighted graph by always expanding the lowest-known-cost node next.

optionMeanings_en: Wrongly linking narration timing to AI generation speed.

Assuming narration timing doesn't affect the interviewer's understanding.
Directly linking narration timing to visibility.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Narration happens outside AI generation, so it doesn't affect speed.
Most interviews don't forbid after-the-fact explanation, it's just a weaker signal.

The interviewer sees your intent as the action happens, making evaluation more direct.
optionDirectness_en: Narration and generation speed are unrelated mechanisms with no causal link.

把审阅动作摆到明面上，面试官看得到你的核验习惯。
审阅本该是候选人的职责，转移会显得缺乏主导。
optionDirectness: 只有输出极短、你已确认过风格时才勉强够快。
任何场景都不该完全跳过审阅。
输出量越大，先声明再审阅的价值越高。
面试官的角色是评估者，而非代你审阅代码。
optionMeanings_en: Skipping review and assuming a long output is automatically correct.
Abandoning the review step entirely.
Admitting the output is large and needs a read-through first.
Shifting review responsibility onto the interviewer.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: The interviewer thinks you're accepting AI output blindly.
Hidden bugs surface later during testing or follow-up questions.
It puts your verification habit on display for the interviewer to see.
Review is the candidate's job — shifting it looks like a lack of ownership.
optionDirectness_en: Barely fast enough only when the output is tiny and style is already confirmed.
Skipping review entirely is never appropriate.
The bigger the output, the more value there is in stating you'll review it first.
The interviewer's role is to evaluate, not to review code on your behalf.

q: 补全沟通节奏的练习方法：
q_en: Complete the practice method for building communication rhythm:
text: 用 AI 解题时录下自己，回看哪里{{沉默太久}}、哪里{{过度叙述}}，几次练习后会形成自然节奏。
why: 沟通节奏很难只靠阅读形成，录像回放能立刻暴露盲点。
why_en: Recording practice sessions exposes long silences and over-narration so you can tune your rhythm.

q: 编码过程中，哪句话属于过度叙述而非有用沟通？
q_en: During coding, which sentence is over-narration rather than useful communication?
options: “我现在要输入 function 这个单词。”
“我接下来实现 search 函数。”
“这段输出用了错误的错误处理风格，我会重提示。”
“我需要想一下这个边界情况。”
why: 有用沟通聚焦决策和状态，机械播报键盘动作只会消耗时间和注意力。
why_en: Useful narration covers decisions and state, while keystroke-level commentary just wastes time and attention.
options_en: 'I'm about to type the word function now.'
'I'm going to implement the search function next.'
'This output uses the wrong error-handling style, I'll reprompt it.'
'I need to think about this edge case for a second.'
tradeoff: 播报决策和状态 vs 播报键盘动作
optionMeanings: 把叙述粒度细到单个单词的输入动作。
叙述即将开始的实现步骤，属于决策级信息。
叙述发现的风格问题和纠偏动作。
叙述即将进行的思考过程。
optionScenarioImpacts: 纯键盘播报不携带任何判断信息，只会拖慢节奏。
让面试官提前知道你在做什么，属于有效同步。
展示你能发现代码库风格冲突并主动纠正。
让沉默变成可理解的思考停顿。
optionDirectness: 唯一不该采用的叙述粒度，任何场景都不该照做。
步骤级叙述几乎总是值得说的决策信息。
风格冲突是典型的应该主动指出的偏差。
思考停顿前的框定语几乎零成本。
optionMeanings_en: Narrating down to the act of typing a single word.
Narrating an upcoming implementation step, which is decision-level information.
Narrating a discovered style issue and the correction action.
Narrating an upcoming thinking process.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Pure keystroke commentary carries no judgment and just slows the pace.
It lets the interviewer know ahead of time what you're doing, which is useful syncing.
It shows you can catch a codebase style conflict and correct it proactively.
It turns silence into an understandable thinking pause.
optionDirectness_en: The one narration granularity to never use, in any scenario.
Step-level narration is almost always worth saying.
A style conflict is a textbook case worth flagging proactively.
A framing sentence before a thinking pause costs almost nothing.

q: 出问题时，哪些沟通动作能把局面拉回可评估状态？（多选）
q_en: When something goes wrong, which communication moves bring the situation back into an evaluable state? (Select all that apply.)
options: 说明当前错误或阻塞点
给出你对根因的判断
解释为什么要改变方向
静默删除大量代码，不作说明
why: 问题本身不可怕，可怕的是面试官看不到你如何诊断和调整。
why_en: When things go wrong, visible diagnosis and explicit adjustment matter more than hiding the struggle.
options_en: Name the current error or blocker.
State your judgment about the root cause.
Explain why you're changing direction.
Silently delete a large chunk of code without explanation.
optionMeanings: 把当前卡点说清楚。
给出你对问题根因的判断。
解释转向背后的理由。
用静默删除代替任何说明。
optionScenarioImpacts: 面试官知道你在诊断哪个具体问题。
面试官能评估你的诊断能力，而不只是结果。
面试官看到的是主动调整，而非随意重来。
面试官看到的是混乱的删改，无法判断你的判断依据。
optionDirectness: 问题定位是让面试官重新跟上进度的第一步。
根因判断把“出了问题”升级成“我知道为什么”。
转向原因把重写和乱改区分开来。
静默删除是这类场景里唯一该避免的动作。
optionMeanings_en: Stating the current blocker clearly.
Giving your judgment about the root cause.
Explaining the reasoning behind a pivot.
Using silent deletion instead of any explanation.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: The interviewer knows exactly which problem you're diagnosing.
The interviewer can evaluate your diagnostic ability, not just the outcome.
The interviewer sees a deliberate adjustment, not a random restart.
The interviewer sees confused edits with no visible reasoning behind them.
optionDirectness_en: Naming the problem is the first step to getting the interviewer back up to speed.
A root-cause judgment upgrades 'something's wrong' to 'I know why.'
The pivot reason separates a deliberate rewrite from random flailing.
Silent deletion is the one action to avoid in this scenario.

scenario: 面试官已经看过很多候选人做同一道题，熟悉常见的死路在哪里。
scenario_en: The interviewer has seen many candidates solve this same problem and knows the common dead ends.
q: 你走进死路时，最应该向面试官展示什么？
q_en: When you hit a dead end, what should you most show the interviewer?
options: 永远不承认自己走错方向
继续微调错误方向直到时间用完
把责任推给 AI 的建议
尽快识别死路、说明原因并干净转向
why: 面试官不指望你避开所有死路，但会评估你发现和恢复的速度。
why_en: Interviewers don't expect you to avoid every dead end, but they do evaluate how fast you notice and recover.
whenOtherWins: 如果只是实现细节的小错，先局部修正即可；只有方向性错误才需要明确转向。
options_en: Never admit you went the wrong way.
Keep tweaking the wrong direction until time runs out.
Blame the AI's suggestion for the wrong turn.
Recognize the dead end quickly, explain why, and pivot cleanly.
tradeoff: 快速识别并转向 vs 硬撑原方向到超时
optionMeanings: 用否认掩盖已经发生的方向错误。
把时间都花在修补根本方向错误上。
把方向判断的责任转嫁给 AI。
把识别、解释、转向三步都做完整。
optionScenarioImpacts: 面试官很快能看穿，可信度反而下降。
时间耗尽却没有可用方案，是最差结果之一。
决策始终是你做的，责任转嫁站不住脚。
面试官评估的正是发现和恢复问题的速度。
optionDirectness: 否认几乎从不奏效，面试官见过太多类似情况。
只有在剩余时间极少、别无选择时才勉强合理。
选择权在你手里，AI 建议不能替你承担判断责任。
面试官不指望零失误，但会评估恢复速度。
optionMeanings_en: Using denial to cover up a direction error that already happened.
Spending all remaining time patching a fundamentally wrong direction.
Shifting the direction decision's responsibility onto the AI.
Completing all three steps: recognize, explain, and pivot.
optionScenarioImpacts_en: The interviewer sees through it quickly and credibility drops.
Time runs out with no working solution, one of the worst outcomes.
The decision was always yours, so blame-shifting doesn't hold up.
This is exactly what the interviewer evaluates: how fast you notice and recover.
optionDirectness_en: Denial almost never works, interviewers have seen this pattern many times.
Barely reasonable only when time is nearly out and there's no alternative.
The choice was yours; an AI suggestion can't carry your judgment responsibility.
Interviewers don't expect zero errors, but they do evaluate recovery speed.

q: 把“AI 输出不符合项目风格”后的沟通链排好：
q_en: Put the communication chain in order after the AI output does not match the project style:
steps: 重新提示 AI 使用项目现有错误处理风格
说明你观察到它用了异常而项目用 error object
继续前先读生成的改动是否符合预期
指出这会和代码库模式冲突
why: 先说观察，再说影响，然后重定向 AI，最后审阅结果，能完整展示控制力。
why_en: The correction loop is observe, explain impact, reprompt with constraints, then review the revised output.
tradeoff: 观察+影响+重定向+复核的完整闭环 vs 直接静默重写
diagram:
flowchart LR
  BadStyle[Output off style] --> Say[Name mismatch]
  Say --> Reprompt[Reprompt with local pattern]
  Reprompt --> Review[Review diff]
  Review --> Test[Run tests]
  Test --> Explain[Explain outcome]
